source.role: English objectives, meanings and progression are anchors; Japanese grammar and scenes are authored for this pair

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Ask the questions you need on any job
lessons.title: Questions on the first day
lessons.objective: Ask who is in charge, where equipment is, when materials arrive, and how a task is done.
lessons.focus: Use 誰 for who, どこ for where, いつ for when, 何 for what, and どうやって for how. Add か to a polite question. 何色 asks about color; どのくらい asks about amount.

cards.ja: 資材はいつ届きますか。
なぜ作業を止めるのですか。

reader.ja: 今日は初日なので、質問があります。
reader.en: Today is my first day, so I have questions.

reader.ja: 班長は誰ですか。
reader.en: Who is the crew lead?

reader.ja: はしごはどこですか。
reader.en: Where is the ladder?

reader.ja: 資材はいつ届きますか。
reader.en: When does the material arrive?

reader.ja: 資材はどのくらい必要で、シングル材は何色ですか。
reader.en: How much material do we need, and what color are the shingles?

reader.ja: 最初に何をしますか。フルハーネスはどうやって着けますか。
reader.en: What do I do first, and how do I put on the full-body harness?

reader.ja: なぜ十一時に作業を止めるのですか。
reader.en: Why are we stopping work at eleven?

forms.contextJa: 資材はいつ届きますか。
最初に何をしますか。フルハーネスはどうやって着けますか。
forms.contextEn: What do I do first, and how do I put on the full-body harness?

speaking.opening: 班長は誰ですか。資材はいつ届きますか。
speaking.goal: Ask about the crew lead, ladder, materials, and first task.

modes.see: Find the questions about material quantity and shingle color.
modes.recall: Recall who, where, when, what, and how in Japanese.
modes.hear: Distinguish 誰, どこ, and いつ in spoken questions.
modes.type: Type 'Where is the ladder?' in Japanese.
modes.say: Ask the crew lead four specific jobsite questions.
modes.write: Write a question about when materials arrive and one about how to put on the harness.

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Say no, not yet and never, and ask for more or less
lessons.title: Not yet, nobody, and another bundle
lessons.objective: Use Japanese negative expressions and compare quantities while reporting jobsite supplies.
lessons.focus: まだ～ていません means not yet; 誰も～ません and 何も～ません pair an indefinite word with a negative ending. 決して～ません means never. もっと requests more; ～より少ない compares quantities.

cards.ja: フルハーネスなしで上がる人はいません。
cards.en: Nobody goes up without a full-body harness.

reader.ja: 屋根の準備はまだできていません。
reader.en: The roof isn't ready yet.

reader.ja: フルハーネスなしで屋根に上がる人はいません。
reader.en: Nobody goes up on the roof without a full-body harness.

reader.ja: ぬれた屋根では決して作業しません。
reader.en: We never work on a wet roof.

reader.ja: 手押し車には何もありません。
reader.en: There's nothing in the wheelbarrow.

reader.ja: もう一束と釘がもう少し必要です。
reader.en: I need another bundle and a few more nails.

reader.ja: 今日は昨日より少ないシングル材を使います。
reader.en: Today we use fewer shingles than yesterday.

reader.ja: 分かりません。もう少しゆっくり話してもらえますか。
reader.en: I don't understand. Can you speak more slowly?

forms.contextJa: 屋根の準備はまだできていません。
今日は昨日より少ないシングル材を使います。
forms.contextEn: Today we use fewer shingles than yesterday.

speaking.opening: 屋根の準備はまだできていません。もう一束必要です。
speaking.goal: Report what is not ready, what is absent, and what quantity is needed.

modes.see: Find what is absent from the wheelbarrow.
modes.recall: Recall the expressions for not yet, nothing, and another bundle.
modes.hear: Distinguish まだです from 分かりません when spoken.
modes.type: Type 'I need another bundle.' in Japanese.
modes.say: Tell a coworker what is not ready and ask for more nails.
modes.write: Write one sentence with 何も～ません and another comparing today's quantity with yesterday's.

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Ask politely and give short, clear instructions
lessons.title: Polite requests and short instructions
lessons.objective: Ask for a tool politely and give clear, short instructions to a coworker.
lessons.focus: ～てください makes a polite instruction. ～てもらえますか asks a coworker to do something for you. Use すみません to get attention or apologize, and お願いします with a request.

cards.ja: ありがとうございます
ハンマーを渡してもらえますか。
cards.en: Can you pass me the hammer?

cards.ja: ここで待ってください。
はしごを持ってきてください。

reader.ja: すみません、はしごを持って通ります。
reader.en: Excuse me, I'm coming through with the ladder.

reader.ja: ハンマーを渡してもらえますか。
reader.en: Can you pass me the hammer, please?

reader.ja: ありがとうございます。お待たせしてすみません。
reader.en: Thank you, and sorry for the wait.

reader.ja: こちらに来て、はしごを持ってきてください。
reader.en: Come here and bring the ladder.

reader.ja: ここで待ってください。
reader.en: Wait here, please.

reader.ja: 屋根の端に気をつけてください。
reader.en: Be careful at the edge of the roof.

reader.ja: 班長は「分かりました」と答えます。
reader.en: The crew lead answers, 'Understood.'

forms.contextJa: ハンマーを渡してもらえますか。
forms.contextEn: Can you pass me the hammer, please?

forms.contextJa: ここで待ってください。

speaking.opening: すみません、ハンマーを渡してもらえますか。
speaking.goal: Request two tools politely and give two short instructions.

modes.see: Find the polite tool request and the instruction to wait.
modes.recall: Recall the words for excuse me, thank you, and please.
modes.hear: Distinguish 待ってください from 来てください when spoken.
modes.say: Ask a coworker for the hammer and give a short instruction.
modes.write: Write a polite request for a tool and an instruction to wait here.

lessons.sourceEnglishObjective: Use Spanish words that look like English and ask for help when you are stuck
lessons.title: Incident words and asking for help
lessons.objective: Name an accident, ambulance, inspection, and hospital; ask for help or a word's meaning.
lessons.focus: Japanese compounds such as 救急車, 病院, and 点検 build meaning from kanji. ～とはどういう意味ですか asks what a word means; ～が必要です states what is needed. The number 911 is retained for the U.S. jobsite in this scene.

reader.ja: 建設現場では、安全が第一です。
reader.en: At a construction site, safety comes first.

reader.ja: 今日は墜落防止設備の点検があります。
reader.en: Today there's a fall-protection equipment inspection.

reader.ja: 同僚がはしごで軽い事故に遭いました。
reader.en: A coworker has a minor accident on the ladder.

reader.ja: 緊急事態ではありませんが、助けが必要です。
reader.en: It's not an emergency, but I need help.

reader.ja: 深刻な場合は911に電話して、救急車を呼んでください。
reader.en: If it's serious, call 911 and ask for an ambulance.

reader.ja: 救急車は病院に向かいます。
reader.en: The ambulance goes to the hospital.

reader.ja: 「転落」とはどういう意味ですか。
reader.en: What does the word 'fall' mean?

forms.contextJa: 深刻な場合は911に電話して、救急車を呼んでください。
forms.contextEn: If it's serious, call 911 and ask for an ambulance.

forms.contextJa: 救急車は病院に向かいます。
forms.contextEn: The ambulance goes to the hospital.

speaking.opening: 同僚がはしごで事故に遭いました。助けが必要です。
speaking.goal: Report an accident, ask for help, and ask what an unfamiliar word means.

modes.see: Find the inspection, accident, and request for help in the reading.
modes.recall: Recall the Japanese words for accident, ambulance, hospital, and inspection.
modes.hear: Distinguish 事故 from 救急車 in spoken Japanese.
modes.say: Report the accident and ask a coworker for help.
modes.write: Write two sentences: identify the accident and ask what a word means.
